the determinants of credit supply by financial institutions to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MIPYMEs) in Peru, which are considered to be the main source of employment and economic growth.

identifying the factors that financial institutions take into account to decide whether to lend money to MSMEs, and to what extent they are willing to do so.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the main determinants of credit supply are the entrepreneur's personal characteristics, the characteristics of the company and its market, as well as the accounting information presented.

the main criteria that risk analysts of financial institutions consider when evaluating a MSME are those related to the entrepreneur, the product or service, the market, the strategy and the organization of the company.

the financial sector is not a major obstacle in terms of financing for MSMEs, but rather the lack of financial culture and the lack of information on financial instruments and the financial sector in general, as well as the lack of financial information on MSMEs, are the main obstacles to access credit.
